title: AGENTS.md frontmatter (v1)
description: Strict JSON Schema for the YAML frontmatter block of every consumer project's AGENTS.md. Validated by scripts/schema_validate.py. The schema is evolvable (additionalProperties: true); tightening happens at playbook major bumps only. See specs/migration-guide.md for v0 -> v1 procedure and specs/dispatcher-chain.md for how the file is resolved.

schema.description: Schema identifier. Exactly 'agents-md/v1' for the entire v1 lifecycle. A v2 schema will introduce a new identifier and its own file; do not reuse this one.
schema.$comment: Constant on purpose: an agent bootstrapping into an unknown repo greps this literal to decide whether the file is machine-parseable.

version.description: Semver of THIS project's AGENTS.md (independent of the playbook pin). Pre-release suffixes are permitted (e.g. '1.0.0-rc.1') so bootstrap branches can ship non-final frontmatter without breaking validation.
version.$comment: The suffix regex mirrors SemVer 2.0.0 pre-release identifiers (alphanumerics, hyphens, dot-separated). Build metadata (+foo) is intentionally omitted — AGENTS.md is human-edited and build metadata has no meaning here.

items.description: Pin of shape 'github.com/<org>/<repo>@<semver>'. Leading 'v' optional. Pre-release suffix allowed (e.g. '@v0.8.0-rc1', '@v1.0.0-beta.3') — supports validating against an rc tag during dogfooding before promoting to stable.

inherits_from.description: Ordered list of upstream playbook/spec pins this project inherits, evaluated left-to-right (later entries can override earlier ones — see specs/dispatcher-chain.md override semantics). Typically ONE entry pinning ai-playbook at a semver tag.
inherits_from.$comment: A pin is a tag, not a branch or commit SHA. Pinning to a branch defeats reproducibility: the playbook mutates out from under downstream agents.

updated.description: ISO-8601 calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the most recent STRUCTURAL change to this AGENTS.md. Prose-only edits do not require a bump.

project.description: Project slug. MUST match the repository directory name and the key used in the projects registry (~/.ai-playbook/projects.yaml). No spaces, no path separators, no leading punctuation.
project.$comment: Enforced as a slug so the registry can round-trip cwd -> project -> registry entry without ambiguity. Mixed case is allowed for flexibility (some historical repos used camelCase before being renamed to kebab-case).

owner.description: Human contact for this project's dispatcher. Surfaces in deprecation warnings and orphan-detection reports.

capabilities_map.description: If true, the AGENTS.md MUST include a '## 5 Capability map' section with at least one row. scripts/schema_validate.py enforces the section exists when this flag is set.
capabilities_map.$comment: Default false so minimal stubs don't fail validation. Every non-trivial project should set true.

personal.description: True if this is Arturo's personal (non-team) repo. Consumed by scripts/discover_projects.py so the global dispatcher loads the matching personal add-on (see personal_addon). Team repos MUST keep this false.

personal_addon.description: Path (relative to project root) of the personal add-on file loaded alongside AGENTS.md when personal=true. Example: 'ELIGIA.md'. Ignored when personal=false.
personal_addon.$comment: Relative, not absolute: the add-on travels with the repo. Absolute paths would break cross-machine portability.

$comment: additionalProperties is intentionally true. The schema MUST stay forward-compatible within the v1 lifecycle — new projects can annotate extra frontmatter keys (e.g. 'language', 'ci_system') that older validators silently ignore. Breaking tightening happens only at v2 with a new $id.
